resources.name: KK Content Exporter - Feed endpoint
resources.description: Manual checks of the public endpoint of a feed: GET /wp-json/kkce/v1/<slug>. Set the base environment first: base_url, feed_slug (a published, enabled, public feed with at least three items), unpublished_feed_slug (an enabled feed left as a draft) and max_per_page (the maximum of the settings). The authenticated requests need authenticated_feed_slug, wp_user and wp_app_password (an Application Password); never commit their values.

resources.name: 1. Pages
resources.description: Pages of a feed (steps 1.2 and 1.3). Expected: 200 with items, pagination and meta.

resources.name: First page (items per page of the feed)
resources.description: Expected: 200; pagination.page 1, pagination.per_page as set in the feed (within the maximum).

resources.name: Page 1 with per_page=2
resources.description: Expected: 200; at most two items; total_pages = total / 2 rounded up.

resources.name: Page 2 with per_page=2
resources.description: Expected: 200; the next items, none repeated from page 1; same total.

resources.name: Page after the last one
resources.description: Expected: 200 with "items": [] and the real total and total_pages.

resources.name: per_page equal to the maximum
resources.description: Expected: 200; pagination.per_page equal to max_per_page.

resources.name: Page 2 with plain permalinks (?rest_route=)
resources.description: The same page through rest_route, for sites with plain permalinks. Expected: the same response as "Page 2 with per_page=2".

resources.name: 2. Errors
resources.description: Requests that must be refused.

resources.name: per_page above the maximum (400)
resources.description: Expected: 400 rest_invalid_param, "per_page must be at most <max_per_page>". Set the value to max_per_page + 1.

resources.name: page=0 (400)
resources.description: Expected: 400 rest_invalid_param on page.

resources.name: page=1.5 (400)
resources.description: Expected: 400 rest_invalid_param, page is not of type integer.

resources.name: per_page=all (400)
resources.description: Expected: 400 rest_invalid_param: there is no mode without pages.

resources.name: Missing feed (404)
resources.description: Expected: 404 kkce_feed_not_found. A disabled or unpublished feed gives the same answer.

resources.name: Enabled feed not published (404)
resources.description: Expected: 404 kkce_feed_not_found. Create a feed with the slug of unpublished_feed_slug, check "Enable the feed" and save it as a draft: the editor shows a warning and the list shows "Active, not published". Publish it and the same request answers 200.

resources.name: Slug in capitals (404)
resources.description: Expected: 404 kkce_feed_not_found: the slug must match exactly.

resources.name: POST (404, no route)
resources.description: Expected: 404 rest_no_route: the endpoint answers GET only.

resources.name: 3. Route and methods
resources.description: What WordPress says about the route.

resources.name: Index of the namespace kkce/v1
resources.description: Expected: 200 with the route /kkce/v1/(?P<slug>...), method GET, arguments slug, page, per_page. Missing when the endpoints are switched off in the settings.

resources.name: OPTIONS of a feed
resources.description: Expected: 200 with the description of the route (methods and arguments); no feed is read.

resources.name: POST with _method=GET
resources.description: Expected: the same 200 as a GET: WordPress serves a POST with _method=GET (or the header X-HTTP-Method-Override: GET) as a GET. Parameters stay in the query string.

resources.name: 4. Access
resources.description:
Feeds that need authentication (access "authenticated", or the setting "Require authentication for every feed"). Only an Application Password is accepted: a browser session is not enough, also for an administrator.

What you need:
1. A feed with the access "Authenticated" (its slug in authenticated_feed_slug).
2. An Application Password: Users > Profile > Application Passwords, a name (for example "Importer"), Add; copy the password at once (WordPress shows it only once; spaces can stay).
3. A user with the capability kkce_read_export (administrators receive it when the plugin is activated) in wp_user and wp_app_password; for the 403, a user without it (for example a Subscriber with its own Application Password) in wp_user_without_capability and wp_app_password_without_capability.
4. Select the sub-environment "Local credentials (private, fill in here)" and fill it in: it is private, so Insomnia does not export it. Never write credentials in the base environment of the file in the repository.

Each request uses Basic authentication (Auth tab): the user login and the Application Password. WordPress accepts Application Passwords on HTTPS only, or in an environment of type local (like kkce.local). Revoke the test passwords from the profile when done.

resources.name: Authenticated feed, anonymous (401)
resources.description: Expected: 401 kkce_authentication_required. Needs authenticated_feed_slug.

resources.name: Authenticated feed, Application Password (200 or 403)
resources.description: Expected: 200 for a user with the capability kkce_read_export (administrators receive it when the plugin is activated), 403 rest_forbidden for a user without it, 401 incorrect_password from WordPress for a wrong password. The data are the same as a public feed. WordPress accepts Application Passwords on HTTPS only, or in an environment of type local. Needs authenticated_feed_slug, wp_user and wp_app_password.

resources.name: Authenticated feed, wrong password (401)
resources.description: Expected: 401 from WordPress (incorrect_password) before the route of the plugin.

resources.name: Authenticated feed, user without the capability (403)
resources.description: Expected: 403 rest_forbidden: the Application Password is valid, but its user does not have kkce_read_export.

resources.name: Public feed with an Application Password (200, same data)
resources.description: Expected: 200 with the same items as the anonymous request "First page": authentication decides who reads, never what is exported.

resources.name: 5. Date filters
resources.description: Filters on the dates of the items (step 1.5). Dates are written as the feed writes them: ISO 8601 with a time zone, for example 2026-11-01T10:00:00Z, or an offset such as +01:00. Half-open interval: after included, before excluded. Set since and until in the base environment. Each filter can be turned off in Content Exporter > Settings: then it answers 400.

resources.name: Modified since (modified_after)
resources.description: Expected: 200 with the items modified at or after since. The next reading of an importer uses the meta.generated_at of the previous response.

resources.name: Modified in an interval (after and before)
resources.description: Expected: 200 with the items modified from since (included) to until (excluded).

resources.name: Published since (published_after)
resources.description: Expected: 200 with the items published at or after since, whatever their modified date.

resources.name: Date without a time zone (400)
resources.description: Expected: 400 rest_invalid_param, with an example of the right form.

resources.name: Year below 1000 (400)
resources.description: Expected: 400 rest_invalid_param. Dates go from year 1000 to 9999, the years WordPress stores.

resources.name: Empty interval (400)
resources.description: Expected: 400 rest_invalid_param: modified_after must be earlier than modified_before.

resources.name: 6. Language (Polylang)
resources.description: The optional lang parameter. The requests that use {{ _.language }} need Polylang with that language on the site and are skipped while the variable is empty; the unknown language gives 400 on every site, with or without Polylang.

resources.name: One language (lang)
resources.description: Expected: 200 with only the items in that language, plus every item of the post types Polylang does not translate. Compare the total with the request without lang.

resources.name: One language, one item per page, modified since (lang)
resources.description: Expected: 200; lang combines with pages and date filters, and pagination.total counts only the items of that language.

resources.name: One language, page after the last one (lang)
resources.description: Expected: 200 with empty items and the real total of the language.

resources.name: Unknown language (400)
resources.description: Expected: 400 rest_invalid_param: with Polylang the message lists the languages of the site, without Polylang it says that lang needs Polylang. Never an ignored parameter.
